what_this_is: Items from the Directorate General of Shipping's own published 'Question Bank MEO CL-I'. A bank item is an ANCESTOR, not an occurrence: it proves an official examinable item exists and fixes its wording, but it carries NO sitting and NO date. Bank items are deliberately held in a separate file from QUESTION_OCCURRENCES.jsonl so that they can never inflate a family's frequency_known, which counts sittings only.
source_document: Question Bank MEO CL-I (Directorate General of Shipping, Government of India)
retrieved_via: Internet Archive Wayback Machine, snapshot 20260110080342 (raw id_ variant)
extraction_coverage: 185 of 185 items parsed (100%). Verified by contiguous numbering 1-185 with no gaps.
extraction_repair_phase3a: Laptop's independent table-cell extraction found item 182 scrambled. Root cause: body lines were ordered by (page, -y) only, so the three fragments sharing baseline y=145.5 on page 16 at x0 53.0 / 359.8 / 456.8 kept pdfminer's container order instead of reading left to right. x0 is now part of the sort key. A whole-document scan finds exactly one body row where container order differs from left-to-right order, so the repair is bounded: re-extraction leaves 184 items byte-identical and changes only 182. Corroborated twice from inside the bank itself - item 64 is the same question unscrambled ('(a) Bare boat charter (b) Voyage charter (c) Time charter ... most demanding and exhaustive'), and item 110 is its opening sentence standing alone.
known_source_defect_not_ours: Item 181 letters its limbs a, b, d, c. Those are at descending y in the source and the parser reads them in the order printed. That is the Directorate's own mislettering and is preserved verbatim.
date_confidence_reason: The bank is undated throughout. Only one item (BANK-003) carries an inline sitting annotation, '(Oct-05)', at the end of its text. The DGS filename prefix 201802120345 dates the UPLOAD to 12 February 2018, and item BANK-144 refers to the Manila amendments of 25 June 2010, so the document as published sits between 2010 and February 2018. That bounds the DOCUMENT. It dates no individual sitting.
oct05_attribution_correction: Phase 2 recorded this annotation against BANK-4. It belongs to BANK-3, the dry-docking welding-fire question. The extractor was correct throughout; only the prose describing it was wrong. Corrected in Phase 3A across OFFICIAL_BANK_ITEMS.json, OFFICIAL_QUESTION_BANK.md and SOURCE_MANIFEST.json, and now guarded by check C33 in tools/validate_families.py, which reads the annotation back out of the extracted bank rather than trusting the prose.
why_only_a_subset_is_stored: Only items cited as ancestors by a family are reproduced here. The full 185-item extract lives in the raw intake directory outside git, and is reproducible from the preserved PDF via the extraction tool; the sha256 above pins the artefact the tool was run against.

items.text_verbatim: A ship on which you have joined as Chief Engineer is scheduled to be put in active service after major lay-up and necessary repairs. State, the preparation and trials you would conduct prior offering the ship to the surveying authorities for survey and inspection.

Your vessel where you are posted as Chief Engineer is about to enter a dry dock. State the coordination and exchange of information necessary with the Master of the vessel for entering the dock. Also, list the necessary preparations required along with the delegation of responsibilities to the engineers of the vessel . Enlist the inspections and co-operations you will make with the dry dock authorities for undocking of the vessel.

An Indian flag vessel collided with another vessel off the coast of India, as a result few lives were also lost and vessel damaged. In accordance with the provisions under the Merchant Shipping Act, what steps should be initiated and who should initiate such steps for the safety of the ships and the marine environment.
As Chief Engineer on board stress the issues you will address for lack of motivation, differences in attitude and to increase sense of competitiveness for better management and effective control?
As per the Marine Insurance Act, write short notes on the following: (a) Deviation (b) Warranties (c) War Risk Clause (d) Charterers Contribution Clause.
How many types of warranties are there in Marine Insurance? Give an example of each type with reference to a hull and machinery policy of insurance.

Underline the general procedures followed for flow of information among ships personnel. As a Chief Engineer on a ship having multinational crew, state how the process of effective information to the team can be approached by you and also how a certain instruction received by you from shore office for engine management can be best utilized?
What are the ongoing developments at the IMO with respect to the technical and operational measures to be invoked on board ships for combating green house gas emissions from ships?

(a) What do you understand by “Unseaworthy vessels” within the meaning of the Merchant Shipping Act, 1958, as amended? (b) What according to you is the difference between “Unseaworthy ships” & “Unsafe ships”. (c) What are the obligations of owners to crew with respect seaworthiness?
